excerpts.content:
Creating thread.

So CALLDEST (paired with RETURNSUB) use case is to mark code chunks that are function?

Scan you mention is about static analasys, right, so graphs of execution can be made? How big of the problem would this be if it is JUMPDEST only.

We store jumptable as bits to database and dont do analysis again on already stored bytecodes.

My first thought was that we need to store both jumpdest and calldest and make a difference between them (additional bit of information). I guess we dont need to do this and can make check in runtime. There is still a edge case if already deployed bytecode had CALLDEST opcode present.
